idiom_name: shovel operator (<<) on a passed String/Array; Enumerable#each_with_object
implementation_notes: The collecting parameter is a Ruby core idiom: producers write `out << value` and String, Array and Set all respond to the shovel operator by mutating in place, so `def render(node, out)` is a natural signature and no wrapper type is needed. `Enumerable#each_with_object` is the pattern shipped in core - the memo object is passed into every block invocation and returned - and `inject`/`reduce` (with a mutable memo, e.g. a StringBuilder-like string) is the same contract in enumerable form. `map`/`filter_map` return fresh values and are preferred when one enumerable produces the whole result.
pitfalls: `<<` mutates but `+`/`+=` rebinds: using `out += [x]` inside a method silently discards the contribution.
Under `# frozen_string_literal: true`, `str << x` on a literal accumulator raises FrozenError - build the buffer with `String.new`/`+''` when it must be mutable.
Mutating an accumulator while enumerating it is a RuntimeError ('can't add a new key into hash during iteration'), so the collector must be distinct from the collection being walked.
